Design · Print · Fitting in Norwich

Partial van wrapsin Norwich.

Printed colour where it counts, with your van’s own paint doing the rest. A partial wrap gives you wrap-level impact for a fraction of the coverage.

Get a free quoteSee examples
  • Quoted per vehicle
  • Uses your paint colour
  • Proof before print

Options

  • Rear half
  • Lower sides
  • Colour sweeps
  • Panels plus lettering

01 / The layout

Where a partial wrap goes.

A partial wrap covers part of the van in printed vinyl and leaves the rest in its original colour. Done well, the two read as one design: the paint becomes the background, and the printed area carries the colour, imagery and brand.

Rear half

From behind the side door back over the rear arch, corner and doors. The most popular layout, and the side most people see when parked or in traffic.

Lower sides and doors

A band of colour along the sills and lower panels, with lettering above on the paint. Good for vans with racking or ladders on the roof.

Colour sweep

A curved or angled sweep that runs the length of the van, often from the front wheel to the back corner. Bold without covering everything.

Bonnet, roof or pillars

Accent panels in a brand colour that tie the van together, paired with cut vinyl for the details.

04 / Is it right for you?

When a partial wrap makes sense.

You want more than lettering

Signwriting gets your name and number across. A partial wrap adds colour and character so the van is remembered, not just read.

Your van is already a good colour

White, silver, black and many fleet colours make a strong base. The wrap is designed to work with the paint, not hide it.

You run several vans

Less vinyl per vehicle keeps a fleet roll-out affordable, and the layout adapts easily between makes.

The van is leased

Less coverage means less to remove when the lease ends, using films designed to come off cleanly.

Van graphics prices by package and van size
PackagePrices exclude VATSmall vanCaddy, Berlingo, ComboMedium vanTransit Custom, Vivaro, TraficLarge vanLWB Transit, Sprinter, Crafter
BasicSingle-colour cut vinyl: business name, phone number and web address.
StandardName on the bonnet, both sides and the rear, with contact details on the lower panels and rear doors.
ProLogo, services, contact details and sections of graphics for a stronger look.
Half wrapPrinted wrap over the rear half or selected panels, with lettering.
Full wrapPrinted wrap over almost every painted panel.

Partial wraps are quoted per vehicle because the coverage varies so much. Most quotes come down to the van size, how much of it is covered, how detailed the artwork is and whether old graphics need removing first. Signwriting packages are shown alongside, because many partial wraps include cut vinyl lettering on the painted areas.

06 / How it works

From photos to fitted.

  1. 01

    Send photos

    A photo of each side and the back, your logo and the words you want. Or start in the free Van Designer.

  2. 02

    Approve the layout

    We mark up where the printed area starts and stops on your exact van, and send a visual to approve.

  3. 03

    Print and laminate

    Printed on cast wrap film and laminated in-house, then cut to the panel shapes.

  4. 04

    Fit and collect

    Fitted indoors at our St Faiths Road workshop. Most partial wraps are a one-day job.

07 / Good to know

Before you book.

Paint condition matters

Vinyl sits on top of the paint, so chips, rust and flaking lacquer show through or lift. Send photos and we’ll tell you what needs sorting first; we can arrange panel repairs too.

Colour matching

We match printed colours to your paint and brand as closely as print allows, and show you on the proof where the wrap meets the paint.

Removal

Partial wraps can be removed professionally. How cleanly they come off depends on the paint underneath, the film and how long it has been on.

Vehicle damaged?

We can organise panel repairs.

Graphics look their best on straight, sound panels, and vinyl cannot hide dents or rust. If your van needs some bodywork first, we can organise panel repairs as part of the service, so it comes back repaired and branded in one go.

  • Dents, scrapes and scuffed panels
  • Rust spots and chipped paint
  • Damaged bumpers and trims
Ask for details and a quote Send photos of the damage with your enquiry and we will include the repair in your quote.

Before you book

Good to know.

How much of the van does a partial wrap cover?

Anything from a single sweep to roughly half the van. The most common layout is the rear half, from behind the side door back to the rear doors.

Is a partial wrap cheaper than a full wrap?

Yes. You are paying for less printed film and less fitting time. The exact saving depends on the van and how much is covered, which is why we quote each one.

Can you match the wrap to my van’s colour?

We design the printed area to sit alongside your paint colour and match it as closely as print allows. The proof shows exactly where the two meet.

Can I add lettering on the painted part?

Yes, and most partial wraps do. Cut vinyl lettering on the paint keeps the name and number crisp while the wrap carries the colour.

How long does fitting take?

Most partial wraps are fitted in a day at our Norwich workshop. Larger vans or extra prep can add time; we confirm it when you book.

Will it damage the paint?

Applied to sound factory paint and removed professionally, it should not. Resprayed or damaged panels carry more risk, so we check photos before quoting.
